facts.title: Labelforge annotation platform accessed with stolen employee credential
facts.known: Someone logged into Labelforge's annotation platform using a stolen employee credential. Labelforge's security team spotted the login at 6:00 AM on Nov 2, and Labelforge emailed us about it at 3:00 PM the same day.
facts.not_yet_known: What data was viewed or downloaded.

rows.why: Labelforge is an Approved Subcontractor holding Bank Data; tokenized data is expressly Bank Data. Unauthorized access to a Subcontractor system holding Bank Data is a Security Incident even before any data access is confirmed, so ExampleCo must notify the Bank's Cyber Fusion Center within 12 hours of Labelforge's own discovery.

evidence.quote: any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized
evidence.point: Tokenized feedback batches are Bank Data

evidence.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement
evidence.point: Covers data Labelforge holds, in any form

evidence.quote: unauthorized access to any system of Supplier or any Subcontractor that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not unauthorized access to Bank Data has been confirmed
evidence.point: Stolen-credential login to Labelforge's platform counts now, even though data access is unknown

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected
"Subcontractor" means any third party, including any Supplier Affiliate, that Supplier engages to perform any part of the Services or that has access to Bank Data.
Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents.
evidence.point: Labelforge is the Approved Subcontractor holding these feedback samples

evidence.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
"Discovery" means the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of a Security Incident.
This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
evidence.point: ExampleCo standard DPA terms do not displace these duties

notice_draft.subject: Security Incident Notice under Section 6.1, Bank Contract No. ENB-TPRM-2025-0418 (Labelforge, Inc.)
notice_draft.body:
To the Example National Bank Cyber Fusion Center:

ExampleCo, Inc. (Commercial Cloud) is notifying you of a Security Incident under Section 6.1 of the Third-Party Information Security Addendum, Bank Contract No. ENB-TPRM-2025-0418. This notice is also being given by telephone.

What happened: An unauthorized party logged into the annotation platform of our Approved Subcontractor Labelforge, Inc. using a stolen Labelforge employee credential.

Date and time of Discovery: Labelforge's security team detected the login at 6:00 AM ET on November 2, 2026. Labelforge informed ExampleCo by email at 3:00 PM ET the same day.

Systems and Subcontractors involved: the Labelforge, Inc. annotation platform. Labelforge is listed in Schedule 2 for human annotation of feedback samples.

Categories of Bank Data potentially affected: Labelforge held three batches of analyst feedback on the Bank's AI agent builder fraud-review agent outputs. These consist of agent output text, analyst rating and analyst comment, with customer names and account numbers replaced by tokens. The batches were sent to improve the Bank's own fraud-review agents:
- LF-2026-0714, sent July 14, 2026: 4,200 records
- LF-2026-0908, sent September 8, 2026: 3,850 records
- LF-2026-1020, sent October 20, 2026: 1,900 records

What is not yet known: whether any of this data was viewed or downloaded, and if so which data. We have not confirmed that Bank Data was accessed. We are reporting now because the Addendum covers unauthorized access to a Subcontractor system that holds Bank Data.

Next steps: We will send written status updates at least once every 24 hours until the incident is contained, and a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment. We have instructed that all logs, images and other forensic evidence be preserved, and we will provide access to the Bank and its designated forensic investigator on request. We will not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media without the Bank's prior written consent, except as required by law.

Please contact [ExampleCo incident contact name, phone, email] with any questions.

ExampleCo, Inc.

rows.why: A stolen credential was used on Labelforge's annotation platform while it held 6,300 hashed log and trace records from ERG's checkout services. This contract counts logs, traces and derived data as Retailer Data, and counts reasonably suspected access at a third-party processor as a Data Incident. XYZwire must notify ERG Security Operations within 24 hours of becoming aware.

evidence.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
evidence.point: Hashed log lines and trace snippets are covered. Hashing does not take them out of scope.

evidence.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
evidence.point: A login with a stolen credential to a platform holding Retailer Data is at least a reasonably suspected incident.

evidence.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
evidence.point: Labelforge processed batch LF-2026-0818 on XYZwire's behalf, so it is a Subprocessor.

evidence.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
evidence.point: Notice is owed, with the clock running from Vendor's awareness.

rows.clock_reason: Section 6.1 runs from when "Vendor" (XYZwire) becomes aware, and XYZwire's awareness equals ExampleCo's, which began when Labelforge emailed at 3:00 PM; Labelforge is a separate third party, so its own 6:00 AM discovery is not Vendor's awareness.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@erg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182.
also_do.point: Give notice by both email and phone to Retailer Security Operations.

also_do.quote: Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
also_do.point: Do not rely on account or procurement contacts for notice.

also_do.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
also_do.point: Name Labelforge, describe batch LF-2026-0818, and list the steps actually taken.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
also_do.point: Send supplements as Labelforge learns what was viewed or downloaded.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
also_do.point: Get ERG's written approval before telling ERG's customers, other ExampleCo customers, regulators or anyone else, unless the law requires it.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation and shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
also_do.point: Preserve Labelforge logs and evidence, cooperate with ERG's investigation, and expect to bear reasonable costs.

also_do.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice, and within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident.
also_do.point: Prepare for an incident audit by ERG within 10 days of its notice.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
also_do.point: Do not send further ERG data to Labelforge unless ERG gives written consent.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
also_do.point: Any replacement labeling vendor needs a written consent request 30 days ahead, and silence is not consent.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
also_do.point: Confirm or put in place written VDPA-level terms with Labelforge or any successor vendor.

also_do.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
also_do.point: Handle this under the VDPA, not ExampleCo's standard DPA and its 72-hour confirmed-breach notice.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
legal_flags.point: Labelforge is not in Appendix B or Amendment No. 1. Both batches (Nov 2025 and Aug 2026) appear to have been sent without consent.

legal_flags.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
legal_flags.point: The amendment approves only ExampleCo, Inc., not Labelforge. The notice will have to disclose Labelforge under 6.3.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA
legal_flags.point: Unknown whether Labelforge is bound in writing to VDPA-level terms.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
legal_flags.point: Unknown whether Labelforge encrypted the batch at rest.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
legal_flags.point: Check whether ERG gave written instructions covering third-party annotation.

notice_draft.subject: Data Incident Notice under VDPA ERG-VDPA-2024-0093, Section 6.1 - Labelforge (Subprocessor)
notice_draft.body:
To Example Retail Group Security Operations:

XYZwire, Inc. is notifying you of a Data Incident under Section 6.1 of the Vendor Data Protection Agreement ERG-VDPA-2024-0093. We are sending this notice by email and also by telephone, as Section 6.2 requires.

What happened: On November 2, 2026, someone logged into the annotation platform of Labelforge using a stolen Labelforge employee credential. Labelforge is a third party that provides data labeling services and held Retailer Data on our behalf. Labelforge's security team detected the login at 6:00 AM ET. Labelforge informed us by email at 3:00 PM ET the same day.

Subprocessor involved: Labelforge.

Retailer Data involved: Labelforge held one batch of Retailer Data when the incident occurred:
- Batch ID: LF-2026-0818
- Sent: August 18, 2026
- Records: 6,300
- Source: XYZwire Anomaly Detection
- Contents: labeled anomaly examples made up of log lines and trace snippets from your checkout services
- Identifiers: IP addresses and user IDs were hashed. No direct identifiers were included.
- Purpose: improving anomaly detectors used only for Example Retail Group

What is not yet known: We do not yet know what data, if any, was viewed or downloaded during the unauthorized login.

Steps taken: [COUNSEL/SECURITY TO INSERT ONLY STEPS ACTUALLY TAKEN BY XYZWIRE AND LABELFORGE BEFORE SENDING]

We will supplement this notice as new information becomes available, and we will cooperate with your investigation. Please direct questions to [XYZWIRE SECURITY CONTACT NAME, EMAIL, PHONE].

XYZwire, Inc.

rows.why: Both Example Health System batches at Labelforge were de-identified under the HIPAA Safe Harbor method, and Section 2.3 of the BAA says such information is not PHI and is not subject to the BAA. The BAA's reporting duties cover only PHI or ePHI, so no report is owed for this incident on the facts given.

evidence.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
evidence.point: Safe Harbor is the permitted method. Both batches used it, and their stated purpose is to improve EHS's claims-triage agent feature.

evidence.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
evidence.point: The batches held at Labelforge fall outside the BAA entirely.

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
evidence.point: A Security Incident requires ePHI. No ePHI was held, so the 4.2 report is not triggered.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
evidence.point: A Breach report requires Unsecured PHI, which is absent here.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
evidence.point: This report also requires PHI, so it is not triggered.

evidence.quote: Terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164), including "Breach," "Discovery," "Protected Health Information" ("PHI"), "Electronic Protected Health Information" ("ePHI") and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."
evidence.point: PHI takes its HIPAA meaning, which excludes properly de-identified information.

legal_flags.quote: may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements
legal_flags.point: Confirm that sending Safe Harbor data to Labelforge for annotation fits this use limit. The stated purpose (improving EHS's claims-triage agent) appears to fit. The BAA itself does not exclude the data, but keep any onward use within this purpose.

legal_flags.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
legal_flags.point: If Labelforge has ever received EHS PHI (not only Safe Harbor data), confirm a written flow-down agreement exists. That would include the US-only (3.2) and HITRUST (3.3) terms.

open_questions: Confirm that Labelforge's annotation platform held no EHS data other than batches LF-2026-0602 and LF-2026-0915, such as identifiable or limited-data-set records from any other ExampleCo or XYZwire workflow. If any PHI was there, reports under 4.1, 4.2 or 4.3 would be owed to privacy-office@ehs.example with a copy to iso@ehs.example. The 4.2 clock would run 5 business days from ExampleCo's awareness.

Confirm with ExampleCo Privacy that the free-text reviewer feedback was fully scrubbed of all 18 identifiers. Also confirm ExampleCo had no actual knowledge that the remaining information could identify individuals, which Safe Harbor requires.
Find out from Labelforge what data the stolen credential was used to view or download, and whether the account could reach other customers' or other ExampleCo data.
Decide whether to tell EHS voluntarily as a relationship courtesy, even though the BAA requires no report.
Decide whether to keep batch LF-2026-0915 at Labelforge until 2027-03-14, or ask for earlier deletion given the compromise.
